source_text: But I don't think we have quite done enough work here.  Why would M-descriptive-essay-of-the-stack be selected?  Why would the author refuse?  None of this makes any sense to me.  Explain it tome in Active Inference terms.

fragments.text: But I don't think we have quite done enough work here.
None of this makes any sense to me.
Explain it tome in Active Inference terms.

reply_text:
Neither event was an active inference decision in any real sense. I read click 20's run record to answer this, and both the selection and the refusal come from what the model around the scoring lacks.

**Why that mission was selected**

- **The policy space had one member.** The record shows one candidate and one policy. 195 mission targets entered the field; all but three were refused for having no interpretation, and two of the three were declined for having no class. With a single policy, its posterior probability is 1 whatever its score. Nothing was compared.
- **It was the survivor by accident.** Click 19's interpretation request went to the first refused target that had a known class, and that was this mission. No belief about the mission put it there.
- **Its score was 1.0498, which is exactly −ln 0.35.** That is the risk term and nothing else. The preference C in use is over four classes of relation to the current focus: focused 0.55, related 0.35, unrelated 0.05, stop-the-line 0.05. The mission is classed "related", the model predicts that class with certainty, and the score is the cost of that class. So C says "prefer work related to the focus". It says nothing about work getting done.
- **There was no epistemic term.** The record marks the free-energy term "not supplied" and the class model "unconditioned at selection". Uncertainty about how the task would go counted for nothing.
- **Cτ is in the record, and it is empty.** Steps 1 to 3 of the horizon have the preference "not yet evaluated" with probability 1; only step 4 carries the class preference. So nothing rewards intermediate progress, which is the point you've made repeatedly.
- **The transition model predicted success.** The chosen cascade is two patterns, each recorded as producing its want token. The model gave high probability to the first want being achieved.

**Why the author refused**

- **The action was far bigger than one step.** The want comes from a checkbox in the mission: "A print-quality Futon essay projects `stack-annotations.edn`, applies the typed rewrite discipline, and passes the I1–I6 audit." That is the mission's end state. The machine treats each checkbox as something one pattern application by one author job produces.
- **The author has its own model, and it was right.** It looked, found the annotations source incomplete and I1–I6 all unchecked, and predicted that the action could not reach the outcome. Its reply was "none: prerequisites remain absent".
- **Its reply space was two words.** The author may answer DONE or REFUSE. It has no way to say "here is the first achievable step" or "what do you mean by this?", which is what an agent in your REPL would do.

**What the theory says should have happened next.** The refusal was an observation the model had given almost no probability, so it was a large prediction error. An active inference agent updates on that: its belief that this action works on this task drops, it infers a hidden state such as "prerequisite missing", and its next policy changes. The machine has no state for prerequisites, and click 20's score was the same 1.0498, so I infer no belief moved. It repeated the policy and got the same observation.

**In short:**

| Part | What the record shows |
|---|---|
| Policy set | one member, left over by gates |
| C | about relatedness to focus, not completion |
| Cτ | blank until the last step |
| Transition model | assumes the action succeeds |
| Learning from the outcome | none visible |
| Author's observation space | DONE or REFUSE |

I read the candidate count, the score, the class preference and the mission's checkboxes directly. I saw only the summary of the author's reply, not its full text. Whether the refusal reached the learning ledger I inferred from the unchanged score, and haven't checked.
